'''Daniel Ofir Whiteson''' (born June 17, 1975) is an American [[Experimental physics|experimental]] [[Particle physics|particle physicist]] and professor of Physics and Astronomy at [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI). He earned a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[physics]] and [[computer science]] from [[Rice University]] in 1997 and graduated with a [[PhD]] in physics from [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 2003. Whiteson joined the [[ATLAS experiment]] at [[CERN]]'s [[Large Hadron Collider]] in 2007 and is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. Whiteson is a co-creator of [[Elinor Wonders Why]], an [[Animation|animated]] educational [[television show]] on [[PBS Kids]]. He co-hosts a podcast with [[biologist]] [[Kelly Weinersmith]] titled ''Daniel and Kelly's Extraordinary Universe.''

== Early life and education ==
Daniel Ofir Whiteson<ref>{{Cite web |title=Greybook |url=https://greybook.cern.ch/institute/detail/experiments?id=003882 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250821030956/https://greybook.cern.ch/institute/detail/experiments?id=003882 |archive-date=2025-08-21 |access-date=2025-08-21 |website=greybook.cern.ch}}</ref> was born on June 17, 1975.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Whiteson |first=Daniel |title=Daniel Whiteson |url=https://bpb-us-e2.wpmucdn.com/sites.uci.edu/dist/8/3361/files/2018/03/CV.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241222141928/https://bpb-us-e2.wpmucdn.com/sites.uci.edu/dist/8/3361/files/2018/03/CV.pdf |archive-date=2024-12-22 |access-date=2025-06-26}}</ref> Whiteson graduated [[magna cum laude]] with a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[physics]] and [[computer science]] from [[Rice University]] in 1997 and received a [[PhD]] in physics from [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 2003.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Physics - Daniel Whiteson |url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/daniel_whiteson |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181109194909/https://physics.aps.org/authors/daniel_whiteson |archive-date=2018-11-09 |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=Physics |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
[[File:UC Irvine Reines Hall.jpg|thumb|Frederick Reines Halls, which houses the Physics and Astronomy Department at [[University of California, Irvine|UCI]].|alt=Frederick Reines Hall on a clear day.]]
Whiteson is a professor of Physics and Astronomy at UCI.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2020-07-30 |title=New Animated STEM Series ELINOR WONDERS WHY Premieres on PBS KIDS September 7, 2020 |url=https://www.pbs.org/about/about-pbs/blogs/news/new-animated-stem-series-elinor-wonders-why-premieres-on-pbs-kids-september-7-2020/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250206191529/https://www.pbs.org/about/about-pbs/blogs/news/new-animated-stem-series-elinor-wonders-why-premieres-on-pbs-kids-september-7-2020/ |archive-date=2025-02-06 |access-date=2025-06-26 |website=PBS |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=O'Mahony |first=Jeremiah |date=2019-10-24 |title=Daniel Whiteson: Equipping Kids to Answer Their Own Questions |url=https://students.aip.org/radiations/daniel-whiteson-equipping-kids-to-answer-their-own-questions |access-date=2025-06-27 |work=[[Society of Physics Students]]}}</ref> He is also the Vice-chair of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at UCI.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4" />

Whiteson is a [[particle physics]] researcher. In 2007, he joined the [[ATLAS experiment]] at [[CERN]]'s [[Large Hadron Collider]]. Whiteson, along with other researchers, introduced an AI technique for high-dimensional [[statistical inference]] in ATLAS that allows for more precise measurement of the width of the [[Higgs boson]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Daniel Whiteson {{!}} UCI |url=https://ps.uci.edu/node/2073 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220404180720/https://ps.uci.edu/node/2073 |archive-date=2022-04-04 |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=UCI School of Physical Sciences}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Bell |first=Brian |date=2025-05-01 |title=UC Irvine scientists among winners of Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics |url=https://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/uc-irvine-scientists-among-winners-breakthrough-prize-fundamental-physics |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250524134556/https://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/uc-irvine-scientists-among-winners-breakthrough-prize-fundamental-physics |archive-date=2025-05-24 |access-date=2025-06-27 |work=[[University of California]]}}</ref>

In November 2013, Whiteson and Michael Mulhearn, a physicist at [[University of California, Davis]], had the idea of using phones to detect [[Ultra-high-energy cosmic ray|ultra high energy cosmic rays]]. Whiteson and Mulhearn created an app called CRAYFIS, which stands for Cosmic Rays Found in Smartphones. The app uses the [[CMOS]] chip inside [[Camera phone|phone cameras]] to detect high energy particles left over by ultra high energy cosmic rays. This data is then analyzed to learn more about the cosmic ray that produced those high energy particles.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Palca |first=Joe |date=2015-03-27 |title=Want To Do A Little Astrophysics? This App Detects Cosmic Rays |url=https://www.npr.org/2015/03/30/395800694/want-to-do-a-little-astrophysics-this-app-detects-cosmic-rays |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250620215827/https://www.npr.org/2015/03/30/395800694/want-to-do-a-little-astrophysics-this-app-detects-cosmic-rays |archive-date=2025-06-20 |access-date=2025-06-26 |work=[[National Public Radio|NPR]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-10-13 |title=Smartphone network could track incoming cosmic rays, UCI-led research finds |url=https://news.uci.edu/2014/10/13/smartphone-network-could-track-incoming-cosmic-rays-uci-led-research-finds/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241104144504/https://news.uci.edu/2014/10/13/smartphone-network-could-track-incoming-cosmic-rays-uci-led-research-finds/ |archive-date=2024-11-04 |access-date=2025-06-26 |work=[[University of California, Irvine|UC Irvine News]]}}</ref>

== Media ventures ==
In 2008, Whiteson started working with [[cartoonist]] [[Jorge Cham]]. Whiteson and Cham have written two books together, ''We Have No Idea: A Guide to the Unknown Universe'' in 2018 and ''Frequently Asked Questions About the Universe'' in 2021.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Kwon |first=Diana |date=2017-05-09 |title=Understanding the unknown universe |url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/understanding-the-unknown-universe?language_content_entity=und |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250323151532/https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/understanding-the-unknown-universe?language_content_entity=und |archive-date=2025-03-23 |access-date=2025-06-27 |work=Symmetry}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Frequently Asked Questions About the Universe |url=https://sites.uci.edu/universefaq/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250618214733/https://sites.uci.edu/universefaq/ |archive-date=2025-06-18 |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=sites.uci.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tasoff |first=Harrison |date=2017-12-15 |title='We Have No Idea' Book Explores Science's Greatest Unknowns: Q&A with the Authors |url=https://www.space.com/39085-we-have-no-idea-authors-interview.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250517131019/https://www.space.com/39085-we-have-no-idea-authors-interview.html |archive-date=2025-05-17 |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=Space.com |language=en}}</ref> Whiteson, along with Cham, is a co-creator of [[Elinor Wonders Why]], an animated educational [[television show]] on [[PBS Kids]]. Whiteson chose PBS Kids specifically to reach the children of [[Low-income|low-income families]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

In September 2018, Whiteson and Cham debuted a science [[podcast]] called ''Daniel and Jorge Explain the Universe''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-09-25 |title=A Cartoonist and Physicist Team Up to Explain the Universe in New Science Podcast |url=http://mentalfloss.com/article/558279/cartoonist-and-physicist-team-explain-universe-new-science-podcast |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190209123815/http://mentalfloss.com/article/558279/cartoonist-and-physicist-team-explain-universe-new-science-podcast |archive-date=2019-02-09 |access-date=2019-02-08 |website=mentalfloss.com |language=en}}</ref> The podcast ended in October 2024, and Whiteson started a new podcast called ''Daniel and Kelly's Extraordinary Universe'', hosted by Whiteson and [[biologist]] [[Kelly Weinersmith]].<ref>{{cite tweet |number=1843687858709901373 |user=DanielandJorge |title=So long, and thanks for all of the chocolate! D&J Explain the Universe is no longer making new episodes. But you're invited to join Daniel and Kelly on their new podcast! @DandKUniverse. |date=2024-10-08 |access-date=2024-10-27 |url=https://x.com/DanielandJorge/status/1843687858709901373}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Podcast |url=https://sites.uci.edu/daniel/podcast/ |access-date=2025-06-26 |website=sites.uci.edu}}</ref>

''Do Aliens Speak Physics? And Other Questions about Science and the Nature of Reality'', a book by Whiteson and Andy Warner, was released in 2025. Warner is a cartoonist and illustrated the book.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Whiteson |first=Daniel |url=https://books.google.com/books/about/Do_Aliens_Speak_Physics.html?id=wr9EEQAAQBAJ&source=kp_book_description |title=Do Aliens Speak Physics?: And Other Questions about Science and the Nature of Reality |last2=Warner |first2=Andy |date=2025-11-04 |publisher=W. W. Norton & Company |isbn=978-1-324-06465-7 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ouellette |first=Jennifer |date=2025-11-13 |title=What if the aliens come and we just can’t communicate? |url=https://arstechnica.com/science/2025/11/what-if-the-aliens-come-and-we-just-cant-communicate/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251204190813/https://arstechnica.com/science/2025/11/what-if-the-aliens-come-and-we-just-cant-communicate/ |archive-date=2025-12-04 |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=[[Ars Technica]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Whiteson was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2016 for "leadership in searches for [[new physics]] and early studies of [[top quark]] mass and cross-section at the [[Tevatron collider|Tevatron Collider]] and Large Hadron Collider, both experimental and phenomenological, particularly searches for [[dark matter]]; for innovative applications of ideas from [[machine learning]]; and for nontraditional efforts in outreach."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Division of Particles and Fields Fellowship |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship/dpf-fellowship |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250807035321/https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship/dpf-fellowship |archive-date=2025-08-07 |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

In 2010, Whiteson was awarded a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-02-19 |title=Vanderwal, Whiteson awarded Sloan Research Fellowships – UC Irvine News |url=https://news.uci.edu/2010/02/19/vanderwal-whiteson-awarded-sloan-research-fellowships/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250718194025/https://news.uci.edu/2010/02/19/vanderwal-whiteson-awarded-sloan-research-fellowships/ |archive-date=2025-07-18 |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=UC Irvine News |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He is married to Katrine Whiteson, an associate professor of [[molecular biology]] and [[biochemistry]] at UCI.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rivenburg |first=Roy |date=2024-05-31 |title=A literal gut check: Scientist studies how intestinal microbiomes affect human health |url=https://news.uci.edu/2024/05/31/a-literal-gut-check/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250319131403/https://news.uci.edu/2024/05/31/a-literal-gut-check/ |archive-date=2025-03-19 |access-date=2025-06-26 |work=[[University of California Irvine|UC Irvine News]]}}</ref>
